# Skill quality

Each core skill carries a quality rating on the process map and the flow: a **grade** (A to F) and a **score** (0 to 100). The rating comes from the open-source tool [NVIDIA SkillEvaluator](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator) (Apache-2.0), 1, quality-check (deterministic, offline), run on 2026-11-10 (tool commit `d717f22`) with this repository's configuration `config/skill-quality.yaml`. It replaces the earlier Built, Partial and Gap status: every skill exists.

## How the score is made

| Category | Weight | What it covers (the tool's own words) |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness | 35% | "Frontmatter, naming, examples, paths, and skill-type-specific structure" |
| Discoverability | 25% | "Description quality, trigger wording, purpose, scope, and naming" |
| Reliability | 25% | "Error handling, prerequisites, limitations, troubleshooting, and implementation safeguards" |
| Efficiency | 15% | "Token budget, body length, repetition, instruction clarity, and reference use" |

Each category starts at 100 and loses points for each finding; the score is the weighted sum. Grades: A from 90, B from 80, C from 70, D from 60, F below 60. The tool's default expects the headings Prerequisites, Limitations and Troubleshooting; this registry replaces them (tool option `--quality-config`) with the sections it expects of every skill: Inputs, Procedure, Human gate, Do not (or Pitfalls), Definition of done (or Handoff), 5 points each.

## What the score does not measure

- It rates **documentation quality**: structure, wording, size and completeness. It does **not** measure whether a skill helps an agent do the task; that is the tool's tier 3 (live runs with and without the skill) and the evaluation method of the Agent Skills guides, neither of which has been run.
- Part of the score is the tool's own convention, not a department rule: every skill loses the same points for the frontmatter fields `version`, `metadata.author` and `metadata.tags`, which this registry does not use, so differences between skills come from the other findings.
- Tool and rubric are third-party and marked experimental by the vendor. A grade is a prompt for a review, not a verdict on a skill's content.

## Where the points go

| Finding | Skills affected | Points each |
|---|---|---|
| SKILL_SPEC recommended field missing: 'metadata.author' | 25 of 25 | 5 |
| SKILL_SPEC recommended field missing: 'metadata.tags' | 25 of 25 | 5 |
| SKILL_SPEC recommended field missing: 'version' | 25 of 25 | 5 |
| No '## Purpose' section | 21 of 25 | 5 |
| No examples provided | 20 of 25 | 5 |
| No human gate or agent notes documented | 17 of 25 | 5 |
| No inputs, outputs or purpose documented | 16 of 25 | 5 |
| Deeply nested references in index.md | 13 of 25 | 10 |
| No definition of done or handoff documented | 12 of 25 | 5 |
| Broad description without negative triggers may cause over-triggering | 11 of 25 | 5 |
| Instructions don't mention 'run_script' | 8 of 25 | 10 |
| No documented scripts in table format | 8 of 25 | 10 |
